scenarios.criterion: Given `loom docs check <path>...`, it reports each finding as `file:line: rule: excerpt` and exits 0 by default.
scenarios.name: Checking a file with a finding prints it and exits successfully by default
given: A Markdown file with one style finding
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file without `--strict`
then: The finding is printed in the form `file:line: rule: excerpt`
The command exits with status 0

scenarios.criterion: Given `--strict`, `loom docs check` exits 1 when there is a finding.
scenarios.name: Checking a file with a finding under --strict fails
given: A Markdown file with one style finding
when: `loom docs check <file> --strict` runs
then: The command exits with status 1

scenarios.criterion: Given `--strict`, `loom docs check` exits 0 when there are zero findings.
scenarios.name: Checking a clean file under --strict succeeds
given: A Markdown file with zero style findings
when: `loom docs check <file> --strict` runs
then: The command exits with status 0

scenarios.criterion: The check ignores fenced and inline code and does not count those words toward any rule.
scenarios.name: A fenced code block containing a flagged word is never reported
given: A Markdown file with a fenced code block containing the word `utilize`
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: No plain-vocabulary finding is reported for the word inside the fenced code block

scenarios.criterion: The check ignores headings and does not count them toward the sentence-length rule.
scenarios.name: A long heading is never reported for sentence length
given: A Markdown file with a heading of 30 words
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: No sentence-length finding is reported for the heading

scenarios.criterion: The check ignores a link's target but still scans the visible link text as ordinary prose.
scenarios.name: A link's URL is ignored but its visible text is scanned
given: A Markdown file containing the link `[utilize this](https://example.com/utilize)`
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: No finding is reported for the word `utilize` appearing inside the URL
A plain-vocabulary finding is reported for `utilize` in the visible link text

scenarios.criterion: Given prose, the check reports a descriptive sentence over 25 words.
scenarios.name: A 26-word descriptive sentence is reported as too long
given: A Markdown paragraph containing a 26-word sentence
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: A sentence-length finding is reported for that sentence

scenarios.criterion: Given prose, the check reports a numbered-list step over 20 words.
scenarios.name: A 21-word numbered-list step is reported as too long
given: A Markdown file with a numbered-list item of 21 words
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: A sentence-length finding is reported for that numbered-list item

scenarios.criterion: Given prose, a bulleted (unordered) list item is judged against the 25-word descriptive threshold, not the 20-word list-step threshold.
scenarios.name: A bulleted list item is judged against the descriptive-sentence threshold
given: A Markdown file with a 21-word bulleted (unordered) list item
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: No sentence-length finding is reported, because 21 words is under the 25-word descriptive threshold that applies to a bulleted item

scenarios.criterion: The check reports a run of more than three consecutive nouns only if a deterministic check can do it without a new dependency; this feature decides it cannot, and records that decision in its own output/help text and in shared/rules/writing-style.md.
scenarios.name: The consecutive-noun rule is documented as not mechanically enforced
given: The feature as shipped
when: A reader inspects `loom docs check`'s help text and `shared/rules/writing-style.md`
then: Both state that automatic detection of a run of more than three consecutive nouns is not implemented
Both name the reason: reliable detection needs part-of-speech tagging not available in the Go standard library or go.mod without adding a new dependency

scenarios.criterion: Given prose, the check reports words the rule replaces (`utilize`, `prior to`, `with regard to`), naming the preferred plain-vocabulary replacement.
scenarios.name: 'prior to' is reported with its plain-vocabulary replacement
given: A Markdown file containing the phrase "prior to shipping"
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: A plain-vocabulary finding is reported naming "before" as the replacement for "prior to"

scenarios.criterion: Given prose, the check reports words the rule replaces (`utilize`, `prior to`, `with regard to`), naming the preferred plain-vocabulary replacement.
scenarios.name: 'utilize' is reported with its plain-vocabulary replacement
given: A Markdown file containing the phrase "utilize the API"
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: A plain-vocabulary finding is reported naming "use" as the replacement for "utilize"

scenarios.criterion: Given prose, the check reports `can`, `might` or `ought to` in a sentence that also contains `MUST`, `SHOULD` or `MAY`.
scenarios.name: A sentence mixing an RFC-2119 keyword with a weaker modal is reported
given: A Markdown file containing the sentence "The service MUST retry, but it might also log the failure."
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: A modal-conflict finding is reported for that sentence

scenarios.criterion: A sentence with only `can`, `might` or `ought to` and no RFC-2119 keyword is not reported.
scenarios.name: A sentence with only a weak modal and no RFC-2119 keyword is not reported
given: A Markdown file containing a sentence with the word "might" and no occurrence of MUST, SHOULD or MAY
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: No modal-conflict finding is reported

scenarios.criterion: Given prose, the check reports each file's share of likely passive sentences when that share is over 10%, labelled as an estimate.
scenarios.name: A file over the 10% passive threshold reports a file-level estimate
given: A Markdown file where 3 of 20 prose sentences (15%) match the 'to be' + past-participle pattern
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: One file-level finding labelled "estimate: ~15% passive" is reported

scenarios.criterion: A file at or below the 10% passive threshold reports nothing.
scenarios.name: A file at or below the passive threshold reports no passive-voice finding
given: A Markdown file whose share of likely passive sentences is at or below 10%
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: No passive-voice finding is reported

scenarios.criterion: Given a project with a DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md, the check reports a term from any table's 'Synonyms to AVOID' column used in prose, naming the canonical term to use.
scenarios.name: A listed synonym to avoid is reported naming its canonical term
given: A project with a DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md listing `bot` as a synonym to avoid for 'Agent'
A Markdown file using the word "bot" in prose
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: A finding is reported naming "Agent" as the canonical term to use instead of "bot"

scenarios.criterion: A listed word that is also ordinary English counts only in its exact listed surface form, and the check has a tested, explicit way to skip a listed word entirely.
scenarios.name: A skip-listed ordinary-English synonym is never reported
given: A project DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md listing the ordinary-English word `data` as a synonym to avoid, but also on an explicit, tested skip-list
A Markdown file using the word "data" in prose
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: No finding is reported for that entry, even though "data" is a listed synonym

scenarios.criterion: Given `<!-- docstyle-ignore: <rule> -->` on the line before a finding, the finding is skipped, and the report counts how many findings were skipped this way.
scenarios.name: A docstyle-ignore comment suppresses the matching finding and is counted
given: A Markdown file with a 30-word sentence
The line immediately before that sentence contains `<!-- docstyle-ignore: sentence-length -->`
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: No sentence-length finding is produced for that sentence
The report's skipped-findings count increases by one

scenarios.criterion: A docstyle-ignore comment naming a different rule than the actual finding does not suppress it.
scenarios.name: A docstyle-ignore comment naming the wrong rule does not suppress the finding
given: A Markdown file with a finding for one rule
The line immediately before it contains `<!-- docstyle-ignore: <a different rule> -->`
when: `loom docs check` runs against that file
then: The finding is still reported
The report's skipped-findings count does not increase for it

scenarios.criterion: Given `shared/rules/writing-style.md`, it names the `loom docs check` command and states plainly which of its rules the command checks mechanically and which rules remain for a human or agent reviewer.
scenarios.name: writing-style.md documents the mechanical check and its limits
given: The feature as shipped
when: A reader opens `shared/rules/writing-style.md`
then: It names the `loom docs check` command
It states plainly which rules the command checks mechanically and which rules remain for a human or agent reviewer

scenarios.criterion: Given tests, each rule has a fixture that triggers it and a fixture that does not, and each ignored region has a test showing a rule violation inside it is not reported.
scenarios.name: Every rule and every ignored region has trigger and non-trigger test coverage
given: The completed `internal/docstyle` test suite
when: The test suite runs
then: Each rule (sentence-length, plain-vocabulary, modal-conflict, passive-voice, ubiquitous-language) has a passing fixture that triggers it and a passing fixture that does not
Each ignored-region type (frontmatter, fenced code, inline code, table, heading, link target, HTML comment) has a passing fixture proving a violation inside it is not reported

scenarios.criterion: Given a path argument, the command also works against a directory, recursing into nested Markdown files, and reports a clear error for a path that does not exist.
scenarios.name: Checking a directory recurses into nested Markdown files
given: A directory containing nested subdirectories with .md files, one of which has a known finding
when: `loom docs check <directory>` runs
then: The finding from the nested file is reported

scenarios.criterion: A path argument that does not exist on disk is a usage error, not a finding, and is unaffected by --strict.
scenarios.name: A missing path reports a clear error instead of a finding
given: A path argument that does not exist on disk
when: `loom docs check <missing-path>` runs
then: The command returns a clear error naming the missing path, not a style finding

scenarios.criterion: Given the change is complete, every new or changed function has cyclomatic complexity below 7, every changed line is covered by a test that can fail, and no file outside `scope.paths` changes except this run's own delivery record under `docs/features/doc-style-check/`.
scenarios.name: The change stays within its complexity, coverage and scope budget
given: The completed implementation and its tests
when: CI runs the complexity check and the test suite with coverage
then: Every new or changed function has cyclomatic complexity below 7
Every changed line is covered by a test capable of failing
No file outside `internal/docstyle/**`, `cmd/loom/cmd/docs*.go`, `shared/rules/writing-style.md`, and `docs/features/doc-style-check/**` has changed
